newsitem.title: USA: Portland shipping unaffected by high water.
newsitem.headline: Portland shipping unaffected by high water.

text.p: Ship and barge movements at Port of Portland were proceeding without problems on Thursday despite high water levels, port officials said.

"We have high water but everything is moving fine," said Tom Allen, a spokesman for the U.S. Coast Guard in Portland. "There are no hindrances to navigation and there are no special advisories that have been circulated."

Talk had circulated in grain export markets that high water due to rains and melting snow had caused problems at locks operated by the Corps or at the port, one of the largest gateways for U.S. grain shipments.

Russ Sill, harbor master in Portland, said water level on the Willamette and Columbia Rivers were about 23 to 23-1/2 feet, about five feet above minimum flood stage but five feet below the levels seen in February 1996, when waters rose to the highest levels in a century and restricted ship movements.
"Flows on the Columbia are close to what they were in February. But I haven't heard of problems at locks, except one high up on the Snake River that had heavy ice," he said.
Both officials said weather forecasts for falling temperatures and drier conditions by Friday should improve the stability of water levels.

Rains in the Pacific Northwest during December rainfall were between 200 and 400 percent of the normal range of 2.5 to 6.5 inches, which in some places represented more than 20 inches for the month, forecasters said.

They said temperatures in Washington and Oregon have been in the 50s to mid-60s Fahrenheit but look set to drop to more normal highs in the 30s and 40s F with lows in the 20s and low 30s F on Friday. A high pressure system should also bring dry weather into the region which should continue into next week.
Those conditions should lessen the amount of snow melt.
